headline: South Asia: Israeli strike kills Hamas official, wife and daughters
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Israeli strike kills Hamas official, wife and daughters.
- Persian Gulf Region: Iran war live: Explosion rocks Sanaa; missiles intercepted over Riyadh.
- Western Russia: One Killed in Samara Region as Ukraine Strikes Oil Refinery.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Estimates of Russians killed in Ukraine surpass all combined US war deaths since WWI.
- Military Times, 10 hours ago: Estimates of Russians killed in Ukraine surpass all combined US war deaths since WWI.
More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war in Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale war against the nation nearly five years ago.
- Military Times, 11 hours ago: All USS George Washington CSG sailors returning from deployment to be provided ashore accommodations.
Sailors from the USS George Washington carrier strike group will be able to sleep in off-ship beds when they return from their roughly six-month deployment, the Navy said.
The Caribbean - bottom line: ODPEM fiasco could scare off future donors, PNP warns.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: ODPEM fiasco could scare off future donors, PNP warns.
Local and international partners could become reluctant to donate to Jamaica in future national emergencies if confidence in the management of humanitarian aid is not urgently restored, Opposition Spokesperson on Local Government Natalie Neita Garvey has warned. This comes amid findings from a report by the auditor general that the Office of Disaster Preparedness and Emergency Management (ODPEM) misused funds donated for a Government-directed roof programme to clear third-party goods.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Argentina officially enters a technical recession.
- Buenos Aires Herald, one day ago: Argentina officially enters a technical recession.
Despite September's month-over-month growth, poor figures for July and August dragged down quarterly performance. Economists are already warning of “stagflation” La entrada Argentina officially enters a technical recession se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: One Killed in Samara Region as Ukraine Strikes Oil Refinery.
- The Moscow Times, 19 hours ago: One Killed in Samara Region as Ukraine Strikes Oil Refinery.
Independent media reported that fires broke out at two Rosneft-operated oil refineries in the southern Samara region following overnight attacks.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 14 hours ago: Ukrainian forces thwart Russian assault south of Dobropillia – video.
25th Sicheslav Airborne Brigade has reported that Russian forces attempting to advance south of Dobropillia under cover of strong winds were stopped after FPV drone strikes and a minefield disabled their armoured vehicles.
- The Moscow Times, 12 hours ago: Russian Official Warns of Ukrainian Drone Attacks on Utility Infrastructure This Winter.
The comments mirrored warnings from Ukrainian leaders about the risk of winter attacks on energy infrastructure disrupting power and heating supplies.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 12 hours ago: Russian drone attacks car in Kharkiv Oblast, killing two.
A Russian drone struck a civilian car in Kharkiv Oblast's Zolochiv hromada on 25 November, killing two people, likely a local couple, Syniehubov said.
Southern Europe - bottom line: French presidential hopeful Teddy Riner says Ukraine is ‘not our war’.
- Politico Europe, 12 hours ago: French presidential hopeful Teddy Riner says Ukraine is ‘not our war’.
The Olympic gold medalist's remarks on Russia's ongoing full-scale invasion provoked a backlash.

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Iran war live: Explosion rocks Sanaa; missiles intercepted over Riyadh.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Iran war live: Explosion rocks Sanaa; missiles intercepted over Riyadh.
A blast hits Sanaa after air strikes near the airport, as the Saudi coalition intercepts missiles over Riyadh.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Houthis target Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea ports as strikes escalate.
Explosion reported in Sanaa after Saudi air defenses intercept ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Kim Jong Un says North Korea should widen deployment of tactical nukes.
North Korean leader warns attempts to deny country's nuclear status will be seen as "an open declaration of war".
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Two Syrian security personnel killed in ISIL suicide attack.
Syrian forces say the attack in northeastern Syria's city of Hasakah involved four assailants who were all killed.
Africa - bottom line: Iran warns of destructive response if key facilities are attacked.
- Africanews, 16 hours ago: Iran warns of destructive response if key facilities are attacked.
Izadi's latest comments signal a hardening of that position, with the Iranian military warning that any strike against key national facilities could carry consequences extending well beyond Iran's borders. There was no im
- Africanews, 14 hours ago: Nigeria's Borgu district grapples with aftermath of deadly communal attacks.
Residents of the Borgu district in central Nigeria were left grappling with the aftermath of deadly communal attacks on Tuesday. Assaults killed several dozens in the area during the weekend.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, one day ago: Sudan: Violations Against Women, Girls Escalates.
[Dabanga] Blue Nile State -- The Strategic Initiative for Women in the Horn of Africa (SIHA Network) has reported the abduction of 28 women and girls fleeing fighting in Damazin and 15 cases of conflict-related sexual violence against girls under the age of 18 in Blue Nile state. In a statement published yesterday, the organisation has warned of escalating violations against women and girls as fighting intensifies, with thousands of families fleeing their homes and facing growing humanitarian risks.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 16 hours ago: Uganda: Uganda, Somalia Agree to Intensify Military Offensive Against Al-Shabaab.
[Independent (Kampala)] Kampala -- Uganda and Somalia have agreed to intensify military operations against Al-Shabaab militants and explore alternative funding mechanisms to sustain security operations in Somalia. The agreement was reached during a meeting between President Yoweri Museveni and his Somali counterpart, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, who was on a one-day official visit to Uganda on November 23, 2026.
South Africa - bottom line: Botswana: Manual Workers Goes Solo.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 16 hours ago: Botswana: Manual Workers Goes Solo.
[The Patriot] Many ancestral land claims looming Boko warned against his CKGR plan
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 16 hours ago: Mozambique: Management of Quelimane Port Awarded to Public-Private Partnership.
[AIM] Maputo -- The Mozambican government has approved the terms of the concession for the infrastructure of Quelimane Port, in the central province of Zambezia, which is budgeted at over 100 million US dollars.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 18 hours ago: South Africa: How to Survive Black Friday Without Going Broke.
[Scrolla] Old Mutual financial education head John Manyike warns shoppers against buying things they do not need simply because they are on sale. Shoppers are urged to watch out for fake online sellers, check expiry dates and keep enough money aside for December and January expenses.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 18 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Zimbabwe Women's Cricket Coach Mark Coles Fined for Abusive Language Towards Ireland Captain.
[New Zimbabwe] ZIMBABWE women's head coach Mark Coles has been fined 65% of his match fees and handed three demerit points after admitting to two breaches of the International Cricket Council (ICC) Code of Conduct.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Israeli strike kills Hamas official, wife and daughters.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, 2 hours ago: Israeli strike kills Hamas official, wife and daughters.
• Amnesty says Israeli actions are preventing births in Gaza, seeks probe into ‘commission of genocide’ • UN alerts world to danger of Israeli atrocities CAIRO: Israel’s military killed a Hamas security official as well as his wife and two daughters with an air strike on their Gaza Strip apartment on Wednesday. The strike that killed Mohammad Abuelouf, a Hamas colonel who headed the internal security service in northern Gaza, and his family was the second Israeli attack to kill a senior Hamas security official since Tuesday.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 12 hours ago: AJK Assembly sets conditions for resumption of dialogue with proscribed JAAC.
MUZAFFARABAD: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Legislative Assembly on Wednesday offered to reopen negotiations with the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), subject to the disbandment of armed groups, surrender of those allegedly involved in serious crimes and an unequivocal commitment to pursue demands through constitutional and democratic means. The region has witnessed violence-marred protests over the past few months, particularly in June and July, with reports of sporadic unrest in recent weeks.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: Sindh High Court restores dissolution of marriage provision in Christian divorce law.
KARACHI: The Sindh High Court on Wednesday revived a provision of the Divorce Act of 1869 that had been omitted in 1981, enabling Christian couples in the province to approach courts for dissolution of marriage on ordinary grounds. A two-judge constitutional bench headed by Justice Yousuf Ali Sayeed ruled that the omission of such provision was inconsistent with various provisions of the Constitution.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Balochistan CM Bugti warns against anti-state narratives.
QUETTA: Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti said no leniency will be shown to anyone taking up arms against the state or advocating terrorism, regardless of whether they are men or women. Addressing participants of the 28th National Security Workshop, Mr Bugti outlined the province’s security situation, governance challenges and development priorities. Mr Bugti described Balochistan as an inseparable part of Pakistan, maintaining that terrorism cannot be justified in the name of religion or nationalism.
India - bottom line: ‘Could be something good’: Supriya Sule strikes softer tone on delimitation Bill.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: ‘Could be something good’: Supriya Sule strikes softer tone on delimitation Bill.
NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule struck a softer tone on the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, saying her party would examine its provisions and support it if it served the country's interests. She said opposing every government proposal was not necessary. Sule also dismissed speculation about her party joining the NDA or her getting a ministerial berth as "gossip".
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Bloodbath at Rohtak dhaba: 4 men shot dead, diners flee for cover.
Early Thursday, four men were shot dead at Milan Dhaba in Haryana's Rohtak district. The victims were identified as shooters linked to the Sunny Ritoliya gang. Preliminary investigations suggest the attack was carried out by the Himanshu Bhau gang. Police are reviewing CCTV footage and launching raids to apprehend the assailants involved. This incident marks another escalation in the ongoing gang rivalry in the region.
- Times of India - Top Stories, just now: Customer wins Rs 1 lakh as travel platform's mixed messages cause duplicate bookings.
A consumer commission in Punjab has ordered Cleartrip and its CEO to refund Rs 80,340 to a customer named Parminderjeet Singh Khurana. The commission found that contradictory booking messages caused Khurana to mistakenly reserve the same flight tickets twice. After receiving no clear assistance about his payment status, Khurana rebooked the trip, resulting in duplicate charges. Additionally, the commission awarded him Rs 20,000 for the distress caused.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: Stock Market LIVE Updates, Sensex Today: Sensex Opens 100 Points Higher, Asia Markets Rebound.
Stock Market, Sensex, Share Market, Nifty LIVE Updates: Brent Hovers Near $94 As Saudi Oil Attacks Raise Fresh Supply Fears.
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: Kim Jong Un inspects nuke facilities, says not seeking ‘recognition’ from anyone.
- NK News, 7 hours ago: Kim Jong Un inspects nuke facilities, says not seeking ‘recognition’ from anyone.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected nuclear warhead designs and various other facilities related to the country’s nuclear weapons program, according to state media on Thursday, where he reaffirmed his commitment to building nukes and rejected the idea of seeking “recognition” from other countries. The Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) published photos of Kim […]
- NK News, 22 hours ago: Truck driver who reportedly killed 2 North Korean women sent to penal colony.
A court in Russia’s Far East sentenced a 40-year-old driver of a truck that crashed and killed three people in December, two of whom were reportedly North Korean women, to 22 months in a penal colony. The unidentified man was driving an Isuzu Elf truck toward Vladivostok when he crashed into the rear of a […]

SEOUL, Nov. 26 (Yonhap) -- The United States announced its plan to slap new tari...

Asia - bottom line: Why Russian bombers at South Korea’s doorstep raise stakes for US-led alliances.
- South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: Why Russian bombers at South Korea’s doorstep raise stakes for US-led alliances.
A spate of Russian military flights into airspace considered by South Korea to be within its defence zone appears to be aimed at testing the regional US-led security architecture and pressuring Seoul to improve strained ties with Moscow, observers say. Several Russian warplanes, including a heavy strategic bomber, entered the Korean air defence identification zone (Kadiz) on Tuesday morning and approached close to South Korea’s sovereign airspace, prompting its military to scramble fighter...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: As Russia seeks closer Asean ties, Singapore faces a diplomatic ‘dilemma’.
Russia’s push to strengthen economic ties with Southeast Asia could present Singapore with a diplomatic balancing act as it prepares to chair Asean, analysts have said. Singapore, which will lead the Association of Southeast Asian Nations in 2027, was the only member of the regional bloc to impose sanctions on Moscow in response to its invasion of Ukraine in 2022. While Russia’s growing interest in Singapore could open up economic opportunities, observers said the challenge would be to navigate...
- South China Morning Post - China, 15 hours ago: China embeds ‘loyal wingman’ drone simulations in fighter pilot training.
China’s military is increasingly integrating artificial intelligence – including AI-driven “loyal wingman” drones – into its routine training for frontline fighter pilots, official media reports have confirmed. People’s Liberation Army newspaper PLA Daily showed the growing use of manned-unmanned teaming (MUM-T) simulation training systems that feature support from accompanying drones, as well as AI-enhanced simulated battle conditions. In a report on Tuesday, it said an unnamed aviation brigade...
- South China Morning Post - China, 15 hours ago: US says Latin America is too dangerous – unless you are seeking asylum.
In its travel advisories, the US State Department warns Americans not to visit Honduras’ Gracias a Dios region, alerting them to violent crime, armed robbery, murder and active terrorist groups. But for Hondurans, the message is less stark. “Overall, Gracias a Dios is a low-crime, functioning department,” says a State Department background report. The report, and similar documents about Guatemala, Mexico and El Salvador, were prepared for use in immigration courts, where asylum denial rates have...

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Teacher who had sex with student after principal's warning avoids jail.
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Teacher who had sex with student after principal's warning avoids jail.
Former teacher Zoe Jade Hodges has been spared jail time for having sex with a 17-year-old schoolboy who was in her care, with the judge finding the humiliation and loss of career were extra punishments.
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: NT records highest mental health ED presentation rate in country.
NT Health says there are further delays to the opening of a new mental health ward at Royal Darwin Hospital, as a national report shows mental health emergency department presentations in the NT are double national rate.
- ABC News Australia, 2 hours ago: Kurtley Beale back in Wallabies team for first time in five years.
The return of Kurtley Beale to the Wallabies team for cap number 96 after a five-year absence is a reward for his continuing excellence, coach Les Kiss insists.
- ABC News Australia, 2 hours ago: Fears for beloved blue groper injured in suspected spearfishing attack.
An eastern blue groper estimated to be more than 30 years old has gone missing from its habit in Mollymook, days after being discovered with injuries from a suspected spearfishing attack.

This briefing is compiled automatically from regional news feeds and has not been cross-referenced by an editor. Treat single-source claims as unconfirmed. I will be back with the next update.
